explanation:
Launches are queued and return at once. Ordinary `cudaMemcpy` runs in the same (default) stream, so it waits for the
kernel. Errors *during* the kernel (an illegal address) appear at a later synchronizing call, not at the launch. An
invalid configuration (more than 1024 threads per block) is detected at launch and reported by
`cudaGetLastError()`. Blocks run in any order, possibly at the same time, which is why they must not depend on
each other.
